A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRIN research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original property-prediction experiments on six polymer datasets, repeat-size evaluations, ablations and embedding visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, computational-efficiency measurements and an embedding-invariance evaluation on unlabeled polymers.

M1.justification: GRIN retains the same residual max-aggregation update, L1-regularized objective and default augmentation using one and three repeating units. Revised MST explanations and the correction to Prim's reference recurrence do not establish a change to GRIN's procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 12,764 unlabeled polymers using checkpoints trained on GlassTemp (Appendices A.2 and D.2). This extends evaluation beyond the labeled collections, while retaining all six property-prediction datasets and tasks. The PDFs do not establish broader chemical-domain coverage for the new collection.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds actual comparisons against GAT and GraphGPS on MeltingTemp and O2Perm at Test1 and Test60. The original comparison methods remain; the expansion is limited to two retained tasks.

E3.justification: New protocols include transferring GlassTemp checkpoints and measuring cosine similarity between one- and sixty-unit embeddings, plus a MeltingTemp efficiency comparison using a common GCN backbone and reportedly identical hyperparameters. Existing data splits, prediction metrics, augmentation settings and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C and D.2 add focused analyses of training cost and quantitative embedding invariance on unlabeled polymers. Existing repeat-size, merge-ratio, aggregator and baseline-augmentation ablations are retained, as are the t-SNE visualizations.

E5.justification: Appendix B in both versions specifies mean and standard deviation over three random initializations. The new result tables do not document an increased run count, a different uncertainty estimator, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing table values are retained, with the formerly blank GCN-based IRM IP/Test1 cells filled as R2 < 0 and RMSE > 1 in Table 4. New tables add GAT/GraphGPS scores, efficiency measurements and unlabeled-polymer cosine similarities: GRIN 0.999±0.000, GCN 0.672±0.119 and BFGCN 0.903±0.060. These extend the reported evidence without demonstrating a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation (2) corrects Prim's recurrence by retaining previously selected vertices through a logical OR with the previous membership state; v1 set every nonselected vertex to zero. The hyperchain definition and both propositions retain their mathematical substance. The expanded Lipschitz explanation restates the existing assumption.

C1.justification: The introduction changes direct MST alignment language to drawing inspiration from MST and heuristically encouraging alignment. This partially qualifies the claimed connection, although inherited generalization guarantees are still asserted. The principal novelty, three-unit minimality and predictive-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning scarce labeled data, the partial evidence supplied by unlabeled embedding comparisons, and augmentation's computational overhead (Appendix E). It also revises the max-aggregation explanation from selecting whole nodes toward feature-level selection and a sparsity-encouraged MST-like backbone.

D1.justification: The new efficiency study supplies previously absent runtime and peak-memory information, including 763.58 seconds and 557 MiB for GRIN. Existing software, hardware, hyperparameters, regularization warm-up and code-source disclosures in Appendix B are retained. The unlabeled collection's provenance is not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for graph diffusion transformers, GAT and GraphGPS, and briefly positions the latter two as comparators offering long-range interactions and global feature mixing. The existing related-work discussion and principal research positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory edits, converts research questions and result discussions into bullet lists, and subdivides appendix material around labeled/unlabeled data and effectiveness/invariance. It also updates the publication footer. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables for efficiency, additional baselines and embedding similarity. Existing tables are retained with relocation and renumbering; all four figures retain their graphics. Figure 2 receives an expanded caption, and float placement and spacing change without a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens evaluation through additional architecture comparisons, direct embedding-invariance measurements and resource-cost reporting, while adding explicit limitations and correcting Prim's recurrence. The gains are constrained by missing unlabeled-data provenance and Table 7's GIN label despite GRIN values matching the GCN rows in Tables 2–3. The central method and previously reported findings remain intact.
